alloy.preparation: Starting 2-mm annealed sheet cut to 10-mm circular discs; one side polished to 1-µm diamond finish. Teflon specimen holder or protective epoxy on edges/back for electrochemical measurement.
alloy.microstructure: Annealed austenitic UNS S30100 stainless steel.

test_solution.preparation: Initially 0.1 M sodium sulphate; chloride introduced after 30 min to produce 0.6 M sodium chloride. Purge conditions are not independently specified for Figure 4.

test_method.procedure_description: Maintain +500 mV (SCE) in 0.1 M sodium sulphate; add chloride at the 30-min mark and monitor anodic current with time. Control breakdown occurs within one minute after chloride addition; implanted sample #9 breaks down slightly later with a much slower current increase.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Sharp increase in anodic current after chloride addition at the fixed potential. The supplied anchor is an upper bound on onset, not a swept threshold.

experiments.result_note: Pit initiation after chloride addition during a 500 mV hold supports an upper limit, not a measured threshold at 500 mV. Control breaks down within one minute; implanted sample only a little later. This is separate from the scanned sample #10. Room temperature describes ion implantation, not a numerical electrolyte test temperature. No pH or chloride-ion concentration is calculated from the salt recipe.

alloy.preparation: Starting 2-mm annealed sheet cut to 10-mm circular discs; one side polished to 1-µm diamond finish. Teflon specimen holder or protective epoxy on edges/back for electrochemical measurement. Mo-ion implanted at room temperature at 140 keV (sample #9); retained dose 3.1 × 10¹⁶ cm⁻². Raster beam over 30 cm² at 10⁻⁶ A/cm²; heated Mo-wire source with oxygen to improve ionization.

test_method.pitting_criterion: Apparent critical pitting potential Ec at the annotated passive-breakdown transition. Authors emphasize poor reproducibility of its shift with implantation.

experiments.result_note: Approximate reading of the explicitly Ec-labeled transition.
